findings.summary: `TemplateRegistry.is_empty` and `TemplateRegistry.clear` (declared at lines 27-28, implemented at `jac/jaclang/project/impl/template_registry.impl.jac:107-113`) have zero callers anywhere. I grepped the whole repo for `registry.clear`, `registry.is_empty`, `get_template_registry().` and bare `.clear()`/`is_empty()`: the only `registry.clear()` hit is `jac/tests/runtimelib/client/test_react_native_target.jac:28`, which operates on the unrelated client *target* registry from `jaclang.runtimelib.client.targets.registry`; every `is_empty()` call site resolves to `DependencyPlan.is_empty` (`cli/commands/impl/project.impl.jac:873,1145`), `CapabilityClosure.is_empty` (test_capabilities.jac), `Changeset.is_empty` or `SchemaRules.is_empty` — none to `TemplateRegistry`. The registry is a process-global singleton (`glob _registry` at template_registry.jac:31) that is only ever populated by `initialize_template_registry`, never emptied or probed.

`ProviderRegistry.clear` (lines 606-609) has no callers. I grepped the whole repo for `registry.clear`, `_registry.clear`, `get_provider_registry().` and bare `.clear()`: the provider-registry hits are only `get_provider_registry().register(...)` (test_dependencies.jac:1078,1125), `.get_by_flag("--npm")` (runtimelib/client/cli.jac:285), `.get("python")` (providers.jac:624) and `.all()` (cli/commands/impl/project.impl.jac:892). The one `registry.clear()` in the tree (`jac/tests/runtimelib/client/test_react_native_target.jac:28`) targets the client *target* registry from `jaclang.runtimelib.client.targets.registry`, and the `__jac_sv._registry.clear()` calls in `jaclang/scale/tests/data/test_eager_spawn.jac` are a plain dict. Test teardown here uses `reset_provider_registry()` (providers.jac:631) instead, which nulls the singleton outright — that function is the live reset path and must stay.
